name: N.R. Narayana Murthy
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, Infosys; principal of family office Catamaran Ventures
profile: Co-founded Infosys in 1981 with six colleagues and Rs 10,000 from his wife Sudha; CEO 1981-2002, chairman to 2011, briefly returned 2013-14. Still a minority Infosys shareholder; his family office Catamaran (est. ~2009) invests in startups and, increasingly, manufacturing, AI and data-centre-related opportunities.
interesting_fact: He says being arrested and expelled in 1974 at a border town near the Yugoslav-Bulgarian border while hitchhiking through Europe turned him from a 'confused leftist' into a 'compassionate capitalist'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Infosys, as chief systems programmer at IIM Ahmedabad he worked on India's first time-sharing computer system and wrote a BASIC interpreter for ECIL; his first company, Softronics, folded after about 18 months before he joined Patni Computer Systems.
notes: Family office Catamaran (run by ex-Infosys CFO MD Ranganath and president Deepak Padaki) publishes an office address in Bengaluru but no email; Catamaran's 2025 thesis includes AI, data centres and precision manufacturing - relevant hook for an energy/data-center podcast. Frequently gives interviews/speeches in India.

name: An Sumei
current_role: Co-actual controller (with husband Lin Lairong) of Zhongxing Group (众兴集团), controlling shareholder of Dazhong Mining (SZSE: 001203)
profile: An Sumei and her husband Lin Lairong are the actual controllers of Zhongxing Group, which holds ~41% of Inner Mongolia-based Dazhong Mining, listed in Shenzhen in May 2021. Dazhong mines and processes iron ore (iron concentrate, pellets, sulphuric acid) and has been adding spodumene/lithium resources. She keeps a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: Hurun's 'Zhongxing' is 众兴集团 (Zhongxing Group), not telecom maker ZTE; filings list Lin Lairong and An Sumei as joint actual controllers of Dazhong Mining, whose product line now includes spodumene (lithium) ore alongside iron concentrate.
notes: Very private; virtually no English-language coverage. Best route is via Dazhong Mining's board secretary office (IR email from annual report). Company chairman is Niu Guofeng; lithium pivot could be a hook for an energy podcast.

name: Tony Chen Shih-Ching
current_role: Co-founder and major shareholder, Largan Precision (TWSE: 3008); left the board in 2022
profile: Chen Shih-ching (陳世卿) co-founded Largan Precision in 1987 with Lin Yao-ying, running optical lens design and R&D as general manager; Largan became the leading maker of smartphone camera lenses (a key Apple supplier). He and Lin stepped off the board in 2022, handing over to Lin En-ping; Chen and his wife Chiang Tsui-ying remain large holders.
interesting_fact: Largan, the lens company he co-founded, is now moving into co-packaged optics (CPO) for data centres, sampling to a volume customer in 2026 with mass production targeted as early as mid-2027.
deep_cut_fact: A National Cheng Kung University mechanical-engineering grad and ex-Canon Taiwan engineer, he insisted every new Largan engineer, however skilled, spend at least a month in their first year crouching beside production machines.

public_contacts.value: precision@largan.com.tw (general company email shown on Largan homepage)

notes: Extremely private, no public social accounts. Born c.1949 (age 54 in 2003 per Business Today). No death reports found; still on Hurun 2026. Best route is via Largan Precision's IR/spokesperson office; CPO/data-centre optics is a natural podcast hook.

name: Ricardo Salinas Pliego
current_role: Founder and chairman, Grupo Salinas (TV Azteca, Grupo Elektra, Banco Azteca, Totalplay); founder of the MAAC political movement
profile: Third-generation heir who took over Grupo Elektra from his father in 1987 and built Grupo Salinas: retailer Elektra, lender Banco Azteca, broadcaster TV Azteca (bought in 1993 privatisation) and telecoms (Iusacell, sold to AT&T in 2015; Totalplay). A vocal libertarian and Bitcoin advocate, in 2025 he launched a political movement aimed at Mexico's 2030 election.
interesting_fact: An early billionaire Bitcoin backer: in 2020 he disclosed that about 10% of his liquid portfolio was in Bitcoin, and he regularly promotes it on X.
deep_cut_fact: A Tec de Monterrey CPA with a Tulane MBA, he joined the family firm in 1981 as Elektra's import manager, and before becoming CEO tried side ventures including a restaurant in Monterrey and selling satellite dishes.
notes: Highly public and combative on X (~1.7M followers); politically active (MAAC). Ongoing high-profile tax dispute with Mexico's SAT (Elektra agreed ~$1.9B payment in 2026) - avoid in outreach. Libertarian/Bitcoin/entrepreneurship themes are the natural podcast angle; writes a blog on ricardosalinas.com.

name: Zhang Hongchao
profile: Founded Mixue Bingcheng from a shaved-ice stall in Zhengzhou in 1997 and grew it into a near-fully franchised chain of ultra-cheap bubble tea, lemonade, coffee (Lucky Cup) and ice cream with 50,000+ stores, more outlets than McDonald's. Mixue listed in Hong Kong in March 2025; his younger brother Zhang Hongfu is CEO.
interesting_fact: Mixue now has more locations worldwide than McDonald's, built on cones and drinks priced around 1-6 yuan, plus a vertically integrated supply chain and its 'Snow King' mascot and viral theme song.
deep_cut_fact: In June 1997, while a student in Zhengzhou (Henan University of Economics and Law), he opened his first shaved-ice stall with about 3,000 yuan borrowed from his grandmother, using a shaved-ice machine he built himself.
notes: Rarely gives interviews; Chinese-language media is the main channel. Best route is Mixue IR. Expanding overseas (Southeast Asia, US stores from 2025).

name: Frank Love
current_role: Co-CEO, Love's Travel Stops & Country Stores (with brother Greg Love)
profile: Son of Tom and Judy Love, who started Love's in 1964 by leasing a gas station in Watonga, Oklahoma. Frank and Greg have been co-CEOs since 2014 of the Oklahoma City-based, family-owned chain, now 640+ truck stops and stores in 42 states with ~40,000 team members and an estimated $22B in sales.
interesting_fact: Love's is also an alternative-fuels player: in 2016 it bought Trillium, then the second-largest U.S. distributor of compressed natural gas, which became the base of its alternative-energy business.
notes: Low personal media profile; sister Jenny Love Meyer (Chief Culture Officer) is the family's usual public voice. Father Tom Love died 2023. Truck-stop fuel transition (CNG, RNG, hydrogen, EV charging) is the natural energy-podcast angle. Route via Love's media group.

name: Tatiana Casiraghi
current_role: Co-founder and creative director, Muzungu Sisters (ethical fashion brand); member of Monaco's princely family by marriage
profile: Born Tatiana Santo Domingo in New York in 1983, granddaughter of Colombian brewing magnate Julio Mario Santo Domingo; her wealth stems from the family's SABMiller stake (now AB InBev). Married Andrea Casiraghi of Monaco in 2013-14. In 2011 she co-launched Muzungu Sisters with Dana Alikhani, sourcing handmade garments from artisans at fair prices.
interesting_fact: She and co-founder Dana Alikhani met in London and started Muzungu Sisters in 2009 after travels together; the brand buys handmade clothing directly from artisans in countries such as Colombia, Morocco and India and sells it at fair prices. She speaks five languages.
deep_cut_fact: Before fashion, she trained in photography (BFA in visual communications, photography concentration, 2005) and interned at Vanity Fair in New York; she cites Loulou de la Falaise as her style idol.
notes: Wealth estimates vary widely (Forbes later revised to well below $1B). Royal-adjacent and private; contact via Muzungu Sisters brand. Weak fit for energy/data-centre topic; entrepreneurship/ethical-sourcing angle only. Recent Hola interview (May 2026).

name: Ratan Jindal
current_role: Chairman (and managing director), Jindal Stainless Ltd
profile: Son of O.P. Jindal, founder of the O.P. Jindal Group; brother of Sajjan (JSW), Prithviraj and Naveen Jindal. Ratan heads Jindal Stainless, India's largest stainless-steel producer and a major exporter, and in 2006 set up the group's Dubai (Jindal Stainless FZE) and London arms, which fits Hurun listing him under the UAE.
interesting_fact: He pitches Jindal Stainless as a front-runner in circular, scrap-based stainless production, writing that 'the world is quickly transitioning towards circularity in production processes' and committing to power growth with renewables.
deep_cut_fact: In 2006 he was put in charge of the group's global foray, heading newly formed subsidiaries in Dubai (Jindal Stainless FZE) and London as their CEO.

public_contacts.value: sonal.singh@jindalstainless.com (Jindal Stainless media contact; others listed on same page)

notes: Identity 'uncertain' only because Hurun tags his wealth as 'JSW Steel' (brother Sajjan's company) - he is the O.P. Jindal son who chairs Jindal Stainless; the family holdings are intertwined. Green/circular steel and renewable power are good podcast hooks.

name: Firoz Mistry
current_role: Non-executive director, Afcons Infrastructure (Shapoorji Pallonji Group) since Sept 2025
profile: Elder son of the late Cyrus Mistry, ex-chairman of Tata Sons, who died in a 2022 car crash; he inherited part of the family's ~18.4% Tata Sons stake. A Yale liberal-arts graduate (29 in 2025), he had worked on strategy, HR and governance projects at the Shapoorji Pallonji Group before joining the board of its listed engineering arm Afcons in his first operating-company directorship.
interesting_fact: His Afcons board seat (Sept 2025) marked the formal entry of the next Mistry generation into SP Group operating companies, joining cousin Pallon Mistry; Afcons builds tunnels, metros, bridges, ports and energy infrastructure in India and abroad.
deep_cut_fact: He studied liberal arts at Yale University rather than engineering or finance before joining the family's construction group.
notes: Very private, no known public social accounts; listed by Forbes as Ireland-resident (family holds Irish citizenship). Avoid the father's death and Tata boardroom disputes in outreach. Route via Afcons corporate communications.

name: Kei Hoi Pang
current_role: Founder and chairman, Logan Group (HKEX: 3380), Shenzhen-based property developer
profile: Kei Hoi Pang (纪海鹏) founded Logan in Shantou, Guangdong in 1996 (as Shantou Longguang Jian'an), moved its HQ to Shenzhen in 2003 with his brother, and listed it in Hong Kong in 2013. Logan grew into a major Greater Bay Area residential developer; since 2022 it has been working through offshore and onshore debt restructurings amid China's property downturn.
interesting_fact: Logan started in 1996 with urban-village redevelopment in Shantou and became known early for a fast-turnover development model, before relocating to Shenzhen and expanding across the Greater Bay Area.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Logan he traded medical equipment and building materials in Shantou; Logan's prospectus says his start-up capital came from personal savings built in earlier construction work.
notes: Very low public profile. Company in prolonged debt restructuring - sensitive; avoid in outreach. Daughter is also an executive director. A third-party site lists ir@logan.com.cn but it was not confirmed on an official page, so omitted.

name: Donald L. Bren
current_role: Chairman and sole owner, The Irvine Company (Newport Beach, California)
profile: After three years as a Marine Corps officer, Bren borrowed $10,000 in 1958 to build his first house in Newport Beach, founded the Bren Company, and in 1983 became principal and later sole owner of the Irvine Company. Now 94, he controls a master-planned real estate empire of ~129M sq ft (590+ office buildings, 65,000 apartments) and is America's richest real estate developer.
interesting_fact: More than 57,000 acres of the historic Irvine Ranch have been set aside as permanent open space and parkland under his stewardship.
deep_cut_fact: Inspired as a young man by a Popular Science article on space-based solar power, he suggested in 2011 that Caltech research it and funded the Space Solar Power Project, whose prototype launched to orbit and beamed power in space in 2023.
notes: Famously private, rarely gives interviews. Input row reflects an old Forbes 1997-98 listing; his current wealth is far higher (~$19B). Caltech space-solar funding is an outstanding energy-podcast hook. Also a skier who attended University of Washington on a ski scholarship (per profiles).

name: Hussain Binghatti Aljbori
current_role: Founder, Binghatti (Dubai real estate developer); son Muhammad Binghatti now chairs the company
profile: Emirati entrepreneur who founded Binghatti in Dubai in 2008, starting as a contractor before becoming a vertically integrated developer of distinctive residential towers. He owns 100% of the firm, which has launched branded towers with Mercedes-Benz, Bugatti and Jacob & Co and raised $500M in sukuk in 2024; day-to-day leadership has passed to his son Muhammad.
interesting_fact: Binghatti built the Bugatti- and Mercedes-Benz-branded residential towers in Dubai, among the first car-brand residences in the region, and became one of the UAE's biggest developers by launches.
deep_cut_fact: He named the company after his late father, Ghatti Bin Ghaeb, and holds a PhD in Industrial Technology and an MSc from the Cranfield Institute of Technology in the UK.
notes: Founder keeps a low profile; son Muhammad Binghatti is the public face and gives frequent interviews - likely the better route. Uses title 'Dr.' Name spellings vary (BinGhatti, Aljbouri).

name: John Stanton
current_role: Chairman and managing partner, Seattle Mariners; founder/chairman, Trilogy Equity Partners; director of Microsoft and Costco
profile: Wireless pioneer who was an early McCaw Cellular executive (COO/vice chairman), then founded Western Wireless in 1994, whose spin-off VoiceStream became T-Mobile USA after Deutsche Telekom bought it. He later built Trilogy International (Latin American and NZ carriers) and Trilogy Equity Partners, and has led the Mariners ownership group since 2016.
interesting_fact: He has helmed or co-led four of the top U.S. wireless operators, and lived in the Seattle area nearly all his life apart from university; in 2025 he was enshrined in the Little League Hall of Excellence.
deep_cut_fact: He got into wireless by volunteering in 1980, as a young Ernst & Whinney consultant in Tacoma, for a mobile-telecom regulatory docket nobody else wanted; one of the clients he recruited was Craig McCaw. Also: he didn't make his high-school baseball team.
notes: Accessible to Seattle tech media (GeekWire Startup Day speaker, podcast guest) - good precedent for a podcast ask. Route via Mariners communications or Trilogy Equity Partners. Whitman College '77, Harvard MBA '79.

name: Jiang Yintai
current_role: Chairman, Shanghai Daimay Automotive Interior Co. (SSE: 603730)
profile: Jiang Yintai (姜银台, b. 1950) set up Daimay on Daishan island, Zhoushan, Zhejiang in 1982 and moved HQ to Shanghai in 2002; he and son Jiang Ming are actual controllers. Daimay is the world's No.1 sun-visor maker by share and also makes headrests, armrests and integrated headliner systems for GM, Ford, Tesla and others, with plants in Mexico, the US, France and Vietnam.
interesting_fact: Over 86% of Daimay's 2024 revenue came from outside China; in Nov 2025 the auto-parts maker set up a RMB100M robotics subsidiary, Shanghai Daimay Robot Technology.
deep_cut_fact: Before Daimay he ran the Zhejiang Daishan Foam General Factory (岱山泡沫总厂) as factory director; he was named an outstanding Zhejiang entrepreneur in 2011 and served as a Zhoushan People's Congress deputy.
notes: Low profile, Chinese-language only. Route via board secretary / IR office. Robotics pivot and North American manufacturing footprint are possible hooks.

name: Clayton Zekelman
current_role: Co-owner, Zekelman Industries; owner/president of Windsor ISP MNSi Telecom (Managed Network Systems) and Nexicom
profile: One of three brothers (with Barry and Alan) who split ownership of Zekelman Industries, one of North America's largest steel pipe and tube makers (Atlas Tube, Wheatland Tube), which they sold to Carlyle in 2006 and bought back in 2011. Clayton, a former Atlas Tube Canada VP, focuses on telecom: he runs Windsor fibre ISP MNSi and bought Central Ontario's Nexicom in 2016.
interesting_fact: Beyond steel, he built his own telecom business: MNSi, Windsor's local ISP since 1995, committed ~$35M to a 1 Gbps fibre network; 'We want to build our own networks so we're not forced to rely on the incumbent networks,' he told CBC.
deep_cut_fact: In 2016 he bought Nexicom, a Millbrook/Kawarthas, Ontario telecom that the Downs family had owned for 75 years, keeping it as a separate company rather than merging it into MNSi.
notes: Low profile; brother Barry is Zekelman Industries' public face (chairman/CEO). Clayton's ISP/fibre and network-operator background is a strong fit for a data-centre/infrastructure podcast. Zekelman family are notable donors to St. Clair College and University of Windsor.

name: Bruce Toll
current_role: Principal, BET Investments; co-founder of Toll Brothers
profile: Co-founded luxury homebuilder Toll Brothers with brother Bob in 1967, serving as president until 1998 and later vice chairman; the company went public in 1986 and now builds in 60+ U.S. markets. Through BET Investments he owns and develops millions of square feet of office, industrial and retail space plus thousands of apartments, and holds stakes in auto dealerships, biotech and other ventures.
interesting_fact: He chairs Lehigh Natural Resources, described by his firm as the largest anthracite coal mine in Pennsylvania, and previously chaired the group that bought the Philadelphia Inquirer in 2006.
deep_cut_fact: He co-founded and was largest shareholder of UbiquiTel, a Sprint PCS wireless affiliate that Sprint acquired in 2006, and was the largest investor in Fifth Street Capital; he also owns Reedman-Toll Auto World in Langhorne, PA.
notes: Born 1943; University of Miami BA 1965. Brother Bob died 2022. Diverse investor (coal, telecom, industrial real estate) - energy/infrastructure angle via Lehigh anthracite and industrial space. Best route: BET Investments office (Bucks County, PA).

name: Malvinder
current_role: Former CEO/MD of Ranbaxy and former promoter of Fortis Healthcare; no current executive role found
profile: Malvinder Mohan Singh, grandson of Ranbaxy owner Bhai Mohan Singh, became Ranbaxy's CEO and MD in 2006 and led the 2008 sale of the family's 33.5% stake to Daiichi Sankyo for about $2B; with brother Shivinder he built Fortis Healthcare and Religare. Since 2016 the brothers have faced arbitration awards and criminal cases and lost control of their companies; his Hurun listing (2014-15) is long outdated.
interesting_fact: Educated at The Doon School and St. Stephen's College, Delhi, he earned an MBA at Duke's Fuqua School of Business before running his family's pharmaceutical company.
notes: NOT recommended for outreach: wealth largely lost; arrested in 2019 in the Religare Finvest case (Delhi HC granted bail in that case in June 2023) and other proceedings ongoing. Fortis is now controlled by IHH Healthcare. No published personal contact.

name: Chen Pengfei
current_role: Vice chairman and deputy general manager, Lily Group Co., Ltd. (百合花集团, SSE: 603823)
profile: Chen Pengfei (陈鹏飞, b. 1989) is the son of Lily Group founder-chairman Chen Lirong and is being positioned as successor at the Hangzhou-based organic pigment maker (quinacridone, DPP, phthalocyanine and other pigments for coatings, inks and plastics). In 2025 he took 10% of holding company Lily Holdings and signed a concert-party agreement with his father; he was previously head of the board office.
interesting_fact: Lily Group, which the Chen family controls with ~68% of shares, is one of China's leading organic-pigment producers; his father is vice chairman of the China Coatings Industry Association and China Dyestuff Industry Association.

public_contacts.value: wdm@lilygroup.cn (board secretary Wang Diming, per 2025 interim report)

notes: New to rich lists (Hurun China 2026), shared with father Chen Lirong. Virtually no media profile. Route via board secretary. Weak fit for energy/data-centre topic; next-gen succession angle only.
